observations: The complete sparse dark vertical opening, left/right rails and unequal internal crosspieces remain recognizable against the broad gray right-hand panel at every native scale. No additional hole outside the established framed opening was found.

The generated rails are straighter and more framed, with narrow bright highlights and deeper dark edging. The top/lower crosspieces and unequal hanging bars still communicate the Original sparse pattern; native1 merges some thin detail.
The gray texture and dark rail treatment sit within the range of the previously qualified304b2/304b3/304b5 native boards. This is a side-by-side material comparison, not an actual terrain join.

Exactly three short horizontal gray bars remain below the single horizontal dark-red aperture at native1,2,3,4. The adjacent long vertical strip, upper recessed edge and lower horizontal sill retain the Original organization. No extra aperture or fourth short bar was found.
The aperture remains one dark recess with ordinary red/brown illumination patches. It is not a new animated flame effect; all Source and HD indices240..255 are absent.

Raised bright edges, right-panel shading and the narrow black frame are stronger than Original and slightly stronger than the earlier shallow gray Terrain4 panels. The shapes remain compatible in isolated comparison; genuine neighbor composition is still required.

The wide irregular black cavity, large gray top remnant, lower sill, left internal rails and higher right post preserve the Source damaged-structure identity. The Source asymmetric remnants remain distinct at all scales.

The broken rim gains small chips and cracks. The upper gray slab stays connected to its rim rather than becoming a separate object, and the maroon/red strips keep the original side arrangement. Native1 softens the sparse internal rails.

The tall sparse cavity, pointed upper break and small central shelf/triangle remain recognizable. The right internal vertical remnant and open lower cavity preserve the Source asymmetry; the opening is not replaced by a new regular grate.

Gray rim rubble and fine fissures add relief. The more granular bright red ground stays on its authentic side, with the bottom sill and outer footprint still legible. Native1 merges the smallest remnant detail.
The shorter cavity keeps its high horizontal broken crosspiece, short hanging bits and low central dark rubble cluster. It remains visibly different from304cf and304d5 at all native scales.

The chipped gray outer frame and the surrounding red ground preserve the Original footprint and bottom border. The low rubble has finer stone texture and greater local contrast; it reads as cavity rubble rather than an added enemy, pickup or glowing effect.
